It's friday again, which means it's time for another episode of Zelda Unknown! This week's episode is about Lake Hylia, one of the most recurring landmarks in the series.

Let's watch the episode and get started! Zelda Unknown Episode 3: The Great Lake of Hyrule.

Episode Summary

For Reference: Zelda U World Map
Conrad = Commonwealth Realm, creator of these videos

Lake Hylia is the common ground shared between the Zora and the Hylians in the Zelda series. It is defined by stark contrasts, where the province itself has a calm, inviting nature on the surface, but hides a nightmarish dungeon in its depths.

Lake Hylia's Zelda U Location and Timeline Placement

  • 1:09 Lake Hylia is very likely to return in Zelda U. The Lake in the southern portion of the Zelda U world map heavily resembles Lake Hylia from Twilight Princess. Both lakes are located eastwards of the desert province and share a landmark that stretches through the middle of the lake. This landmark is likely the Great Bridge of Hylia, which appeared in Twilight Princess and in a less developed state in OoT.

  • 2:16 In the Zelda U footage at the Game Awards, we can see what appears to be the southern gate of the Great Bridge. The structure Link approaches on Epona looks very similar to the gate from Twilight Princess, though in a much more pristine condition. The structure of the gate is nearly identical to better preserved Northern Gate from TP, so it is extremely likely that this is indeed the Great Bridge of Hyrule in Zelda U from a different time period.

  • 3:26 The condition of the bridge has some heavy implications for the timeline placement of Zelda U. Since the bridge exists in its completed state, whereas it was the beginnings of a bridge in OoT, but is not yet in ruins like it was in TP, this means that Zelda U very likely take place sometime between Ocarina of Time and Twilight Princess on the timeline. Another possibility is that it takes place after TP and the bridge has been restored

  • 5:45 Epona is another hint on Zelda U's timeline placement. Epona has only appeared in the series within the unified timeline and the child timeline, in Ocarina of Time, Majora's Mask, Four Swords Adventures, the Minish Cap, Twilight Princess, and now Zelda U.

Characteristics of Lake Hylia in Zelda U

The video now goes into discussing the mechanics of Lake Hylia in Zelda U. As usual, it divides this speculation into categories:

  • 6:45 Geography: Unlike previous games, Zelda U has a much vaster network of lakes and rivers and has other large lakes outside of Hylia. This creates several possibilities for Zelda U, including rowing as a central means of transportation, Link having his own personal boat or canoe, and the return of river and lake based mini-games.

  • 8:07 Controls: The swimming and diving controls could make or break this area in Zelda U. It has historically been a problem for Zelda games, right up to Skyward Sword and the most recent Majora's Mask remake. This brings up concerns that Zelda U may follow the same trend.

  • 10:18 Fishing: One of the most beloved mini-games in the Zelda series has been fishing. This has only appeared twice so far with OoT and TP, but with the vast number of water areas in the Zelda U world map it is likely to make a third appearance in this game. Should it return, it should include a much greater variety of fish, and the ability to fish not only in defined areas but in all of Hyrule's rivers and lakes. Conrad also liked the motion controls used for fishing in TP, as they added a great sense of immersion to the fishing experience. Conrad is really, really into fishing, guys.

  • 11:47 Races: Lake Hylia and the rivers in the Zelda series have historically been known as a rare common ground between the Hylians, the Humans, and the Zora. This should also be the case in Zelda U. All races should return to the roles they had in previous games, running mini-games around the lakes and rivers, with the Zora being racing buddies and diving games like in OoT. The Zora should have a much larger role in Zelda U than in previous entries, appearing outside of Zora's domain in all the water areas of Hyrule.

  • 13:12 Villages: The rivers and lakes of Hyrule should be populated by at least some smaller fishing villages with fish markets where you can buy and sell fish that serve some purpose to the game. You could also rent or buy your canoe here for traveling along Hyrule's extensive new river network, and fishing in. This village should also have bait shops, where you can buy different baits, reels and rods to improve your fishing experience. Conrad is really into fishing, guys.

  • 14:00 Dungeon: Since the introduction of the first water dungeon in Ocarina of Time, Water temples have had a notorious reputation in the Zelda series. Both the water dungeons in Ocarina of Time and Twilight Princess were host to tedious and confusing layouts that tested the patience of the player (says Conrad in an increasingly aggressive tone). This trend was finally abandoned in Skyward Sword with Ancient Cistern, a brilliant and unconventional dungeon with several references to Buddhism. Conrad hopes that the Zelda U dungeon will be more similar to Ancient Cistern rather than the previous entries. With how much water there is in Zelda U, it's possible we may even get two water dungeons in the new game.

Topics for Discussion

These are the topics from the video I found particularly interesting. Feel free to reply to any, all or none of these questions, ask your own, and let us know your own thoughts on Conrad's ideas.

  1. Lake Hylia is described as a common ground between the Zora and the Hylians. Do you agree with this statement? Do you want think it should serve this purpose the same or more in Zelda U, or have a new purpose entirely?

  2. Is the evidence that Lake Hylia is present in Zelda U as the same lake from OoT and TP convincing? If so, do you think the game takes place between OoT and TP, or after TP, with the Great Bridge having been restored? Which would you prefer?

  3. How do you feel about fishing? Does Conrad need to calm down? Is fishing really that great?

  4. This video focuses on the relationship between the Zora, the Hylians and the Humans around Lake Hylia, but does not speculate on any new races. Do you think those are fine, or do you hope a new race populates the area this time as well? Should it be a different race that has appeared somewhere else in the series, or a brand new one?

  5. Since Zelda U's world map is so enormous, there should definitely be many more villages populating it than the previous games have had. What do you think of the fishing village idea? What are some other cool villages that could be around Lake Hylia?

  6. What is your favorite water dungeon from the Zelda series, and what do you want the dungeon in Zelda U to be like?
